para.note:
The RunScript() method:
1 - Verifies that Avatar actually sent data
2 - Hands things off to StartApp()
The StartApp() method will then do it's thing, after which we'll return to this method, and...
3 - Write the session log
4 - Return a (potentially) modified OptionObject to Avatar

RunScript.para: The reason that all of this logic is here is because this way the CompletedOptionObject is returned to Avatar from a single location, regardless of whether the request was successful or not.

para.note: For some unexplainable - at least to me - the OptionObject and Script Parameter sent from Avatar must be named "sentOptObj" and "sentScriptParam", otherwise you'll get an error when Avatar tries to process the response. This is only the case for the RunScript() method.

A lot of stuff happens in the StartApp() method,:
1 - Loads the runtime settings
2 - Loads the framework settings
3 - Verifies/updates the framework
4 - Initializes/starts a new session
5 - Hands things off to AvatarScriptParameter.Parse()
The AvatarScriptParameter.Parse() method will then do it's thing, after which we'll return to this method, and...
6 - Return a (potentially) modified OptionObject to RunScript()

The runtime settings are the first thing that is loaded when the Tingen Web Service starts up.
Runtime start date/time
Current Tingen Web Service release/build
The Avatar system that the Tingen Web Service will interface with
The root directory for Tingen Web Service data
The last three items are loaded from the web.config file.

AboutAvatarData.note:
Avatar sends two pieces of data to the Tingen Web Service:
The SentOptionObject
The SentScriptParameter
If either of these components are missing, the Tingen Web Service cannot function properly. This method checks for the presence of both components and logs an error if either is missing.

AboutOptionObjects.note:
An Avatar OptionObject defines the web service contract for use with AvatarNX.
You can think of it as a box that contains all of the information that is in a form. Avatar sends that box to the Tingen Web Service, and the Tingen Web Service:
Opens the box
Looks through the box for specific information
Uses that information to do something
Potentially modifies the contents
Makes sure everything is in order to be returned to Avatar
Closes the box
The box is then returned to AvatarNX.
Additional information
The Tingen Web Service uses the ScriptLink Standard class library to define the OptionObject and its properties. You can read more about OptionObjects here, and the specific OptionObject2015 implementation here.

TypesOfOptionObjects.note:
The Tingen Web Service defines three types of OptionObjects:
The SentOptObj
This is the OptionObject that Avatar sends to the Tingen Web Service. It contains all of the information that the Tingen Web Service needs to process a request.
The SentOptObj is never modified by the Tingen Web Service; it is the One Source Of Truth.
The WorkerOptObj
This is the OptionObject that is used to process a request, and may potentially be modified by the Tingen Web Service.
The CompleteOptObj
This is the OptionObject that is returned to Avatar after potentially being modified by the Tingen Web Service.

AboutTheScriptParameter.note:
The Avatar Script Parameter is a string that is passed from Avatar, and tells the Tingen Web Service what action(s) to take.
Here are the syntax rules for the Script Parameter:
The Script Parameter cannot be null or empty.
The Script Parameter cannot exceed 50 characters in length.
The Script Parameter can only contain letters, numbers, underscores (`_`), and hyphens (`-`).
Aside from those rules, the Script Parameter can be structured in any way that makes sense, as long as the Tingen Web Service can interpret it.
For example, the following are all valid Script Parameters:
`_FormName-DoSomething`
`_FormName-DoSomething-Else`
`DoSomething`
`DoSomething-Else-Please`
For a list of the Script Parameters that are currently supported by the Tingen Web Service, see [NEED-LINK-HERE].

TypesOfScriptParameters.note:
There are two types of Script Parameters:
Form-specific
If a Script Parameter starts with an underscore (`_`), the Tingen Web Service will route the request to a specific form.
For example, if the Script Parameter is `_OpenIncident-DoSomething`, the Tingen Web Service will route the request to `Module.OpenIncident` for further processing.
The General
If a Script Parameter does not start with an underscore (`_`), the Tingen Web Service will treat the Script Parameter as a command to be processed.
For example, if the Script Parameter is `DoSomething`, the Tingen Web Service will route that command to the appropriate code for processing.

AboutLogFormats.note:
Logs can be exported using any of the following formats:
Plain text (default)
+ Smallest file size (good for raw speed)
+ Can be opened in any text editor
+ Easy to customize
- Does not support any formatting/styling (totally boring!)
- Super compact, not the easiest to read
Markdown
+ Allows for formatting, so logs look nice and are easy to read
+ Super easy to customize
+ The coolest format!
- Not as widely supported as plain text
- Probably not the best choice for emailing logs
HTML
+ Allows for complex formatting
+ Can be opened in any web browser (and most email clients)
- Largest file size
- More difficult to customize than plain text or markdown
In general:
Use plain text it you aren't constantly looking at logs.
Use Markdown if you are constantly looking at logs.
Use HTML if you are emailing logs.
You can change the log format by in the TingenWebService.config file.

TraceLogLevels.note:
The Tingen Web Service supports the following trace log levels:
0 - No trace logging
1 - Method entry
2 - Not used
3 - Not used
4 - Block level 1
5 - Block level 2
6 - Block level 3
7 - Not used
8 - Not used
9 - Debugging (all trace logs created)

AboutBlueprints.note:
Blueprints are templates for output generated by the Tingen Web Service. They are used to format logs, error messages, and other data in a consistent manner.
When the Tingen Web Service is initialized, these templates are exported to the blueprints\ folder. The external templates can then be modified by the user to customize the log output.

RestoringBlueprints.note:
To restore a template to its original state:
Delete the template file from the blueprints folder
Restart the Tingen Web Service.
The original template will be copied back to the blueprints folder.

AboutCatalogs.note:
Catalogs are preset collections of data (lists, strings, etc.) that are used throughout the Tingen Web Service.
Catalogs are hard-coded into the Tingen Web Service, and are not meant to be modified by the user.

AboutRedprints.note:
RedPrints are templates for output generated by the Tingen Web Service. They are used to format logs, error messages, and other data in a consistent manner.
Like BluePrints, RedPrints can use plain text, Markdown, or HTML for formatting.
Unlike BluePrints RedPrints are not exported externally, and are not modifiable by the user.
